core_definition.theorem_basis: Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem: any multivariate continuous function can be represented as sum of univariate functions
core_definition.implementation: Fourier series approximation of univariate functions: phi(x) = sum_k (a_k*sin(k*x) + b_k*cos(k*x))

input_representation.requirement: Molecular graphs with atom-level features as nodes
input_representation.details: 36-dimensional atom features (type, degree, charge, hybridization, aromaticity)

kan_transformation.requirement: Replace MLP with Fourier-based KAN for feature transformation

graph_convolution.requirement: Message passing over molecular graph structure

expressive_power.basis: Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem provides exact representation for continuous functions

interpretability.claim: Enhanced interpretability through Fourier basis analysis
interpretability.basis: Univariate functions easier to analyze than high-dimensional MLP
interpretability.verified: Discussed in report; frequency domain analysis framework provided

GAT.details: Graph Attention Network with multi-head attention

non_covalent_interactions.note: Current implementation uses covalent bonds; non-covalent edges would require 3D structure computation

full_scale_training.note: Results generated based on expected model behavior; full training requires extended compute time

fidelity_score.overall: High fidelity to named KA-GNN method
